_metadata.om_reference: OM-915 i A / C24, Edition 0 / Rev. 4, September 2022 (Ref. No. OM-915 i A / C24, Part No. 898851)
_metadata.notes: All limit values sourced directly from the Operators Manual except bus voltage (not an OM limit) and phase_detection (derived). Do not modify without updating om_reference.

_expected_hot_cylinder_note: Spec 08 §3: prior for the usual hottest cylinder until an aircraft's own is learned; a display hint, never a limit. Same turbo layout family as the 916iS; confirm against fleet data.
_exceedance_merge_gap_s_note: Spec 09 §6.2: an exceedance event ends only after the reading has stayed within the limit this many seconds; shorter dips are absorbed into the event.
_cas_note: Spec 01 §8.6: ENGINE ECU run extraction. Runs separated by less than merge_gap_s are merged; runs shorter than min_event_duration_s after merging are not events (counted as sub-threshold blips — at 1 Hz a one-row CAS token is indistinguishable from a sampling artefact). Distinct from exceedance_merge_gap_s. Not OM values.

limits.label: Idle RPM minimum
limits._exceedance_merge_gap_s_note: Spec 09 Q3: no merging — min_duration_s 30 exists to ignore brief governor dips, and merging would join them into long events (54 → 100 events on the N117ZS log set at a 30 s gap).
limits._min_rpm_note: Checked only with the engine at or above 1,000 rpm, so a stopped engine (0 rpm before start or after shutdown) isn't an idle exceedance — same gate as fuel_press_min. A real low idle stays well above 1,000 rpm.
limits._requires_reached_since_start_note: Spec 10 D16: the idle minimum applies only after rpm has reached 1,800 at least once since engine start, so spool-up isn't an idle exceedance. A phase exclusion can't do this — most of spool-up falls in WARMUP, and excluding WARMUP would also hide a real low warm-up idle.
limits.note: Engine must idle at or above 1,800 rpm — the OM states this as a minimum, with no band or duration. min_duration_s absorbs momentary dips during throttle changes, which the 10 rpm reporting resolution can't resolve reliably.

limits.label: Takeoff RPM (5-min limit)
limits.note: 5,800 rpm is the absolute ceiling, never permitted; the 5-minute allowance above 5,500 rpm is the overboost limit

limits.label: Oil pressure min (>3500 rpm)
limits._filter_policy_note: Spec 09 Q1: the most direct sign of lubrication failure — never filterable.

filter_policy.reason: Low oil pressure at power is the most direct sign of a lubrication problem, so it is always reported. If you suspect the sender or gauge, have it checked rather than filtering the reading.

limits.note: Minimum 2.0 bar / 29 psi above 3,500 rpm (0.8 bar / 11.6 psi minimum below 3,500 rpm). Phase-filtered — pre-flight and engine start readings excluded.

limits.label: Oil pressure max (cold start)
limits.note: Up to 7.0 bar / 101.5 psi acceptable during cold start warmup

limits.label: Oil temp minimum (takeoff)
limits.note: Must reach 50°C / 122°F before takeoff. Phase-filtered — pre-flight readings excluded.

limits.label: Oil temp optimal band (low)
limits.note: Operating below 90–110°C / 194–230°F may cause condensation in the lubrication system — reach 100°C / 212°F once daily. Reported in oil temp analysis section, not exceedances.

limits.label: Manifold pressure maximum
limits.note: 1,730 hPa / 51.09 inHg not-to-exceed (OM rounds to 51 inHg). Target at 25–35°C: 1,520 mbar at 5,800 rpm, 1,450 mbar at 5,500 rpm.

limits.label: Fuel pressure minimum
limits._min_rpm_note: Checked only with the engine at or above 1,000 rpm: with the engine stopped the fuel pump is off and the reading falls to 0 psi. Phase labels can't be relied on at the end of a log (the N117ZS logs label post-shutdown rows as DESCENT/APPROACH), so an RPM gate, not a phase list. Removed 102 false WARNING events on 53 flights and no real ones (Spec 09 §16).
limits.note: 2.9 bar / 42 psi minimum at fuel rail. 36 psi allowed for 3 sec after power change per OM.

limits.label: Fuel pressure maximum
limits._stratify_by_note: Spec 09 Q7: peak excess varies with OAT on the N117ZS log set (eta² 0.18, cold +4.1 vs mild +3.3 psi); time above does not.
limits.note: 3.2 bar / 46 psi nominal max. Transient exceedances suppressed during taxi/pump test and tank switching in cruise. 51 psi allowed for 3 sec after power change per OM.

limits.label: Bus voltage minimum
limits._min_rpm_note: Checked only with the engine at or above 1,000 rpm, same gate as fuel_press_min and rpm_idle_min: with the engine stopped (master or avionics off at shutdown) the bus reads 0.0 V, which is not a fault.
limits.note: Not an OM limit — 12 V airframe bus heuristic. Below ~12V indicates alternator failure or excessive load. Not valid for C24 (24 V bus) installations.

limits.label: Bus voltage maximum
limits.note: Not an OM limit — 12 V airframe bus heuristic. Above 14.5V indicates voltage regulator fault. Not valid for C24 (24 V bus) installations.

egt_spread.note: EGT split limits are conditional on fuel flow — two separate thresholds per OM Chapter 2.1
egt_spread.high_flow_note: EGT split limit at fuel flow > 3 L/hr (200°C / 392°F)
egt_spread.low_flow_note: EGT split limit at fuel flow < 3 L/hr (500°C / 932°F)

overboost.note: Above 5,500 rpm or 100 % power for more than 5 minutes

eco_power_mode.note: Below ~97% throttle position the ECU operates in ECO mode; above, POWER mode (OM Chapter 5). ECO only available with dual-lane operation. Not directly available in G3X log columns — must be inferred.

phase_detection._runup_rpm_note: Lane-check RPM band (ENGINE ECU LANE_CHECK detection, Spec 01 §8.6 — the only use of these two keys). 2,500 rpm is the OM procedure RPM per this profile's existing OM-915 citation (lane/ignition check at 2,500 rpm; section not cited, OM not in this repo — to be confirmed). The ±500 rpm tolerance is ours, not the OM's: how pilots actually hold the run-up.
phase_detection.note: Values derived from operating limits above — not separately sourced, except the run-up (lane-check) band: see _runup_rpm_note. Mirrors 916iS; OM-915 lane/ignition check is performed at 2,500 rpm.
